unit.title: Trustworthy Parallelism: From Sequential Oracle to Measured C++ Histogram
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student beginning deliberate software-engineering practice
unit.summary: Build, test, and measure a deterministic byte-histogram program with a sequential reference and a race-free std::thread implementation. The emphasis is trustworthy evidence: explicit contracts, automated tests, reproducible benchmarks, and qualified performance claims.
learning_objectives: Translate a work-partitioning idea into explicit interfaces, invariants, and failure behavior.
Use a sequential implementation as an oracle for a concurrent implementation.
Reason about work, span, synchronization, data races, and parallel overhead.
Build deterministic automated tests that cover boundary cases and multiple thread counts.
Collect reproducible timing data and separate observations from explanations.

assumed_background.unit_requirement: Working C++17 knowledge, basic computer architecture, asymptotic analysis, and command-line build tools
assumed_background.catalog_conflict_note: The normalized course prerequisites say C, while the raw catalog field and programming-language field say C++; this unit requires C++ and does not silently resolve the source discrepancy.

deliverables: A buildable C++17 project with sequential and parallel histogram implementations
A deterministic automated test suite and documented build/test commands
A short design note stating contracts, decomposition, and concurrency risks
Raw benchmark data plus a concise analysis that qualifies all performance claims
Written responses to the learner-safe comprehension prompts
out_of_scope: CUDA, MPI, OpenMP, Spark, distributed execution, and GPU optimization
Reproduction of any Stanford CS149 or CMU 15-418 assignment
Expansion of catalog links into an official lecture or assignment sequence
Any claim that this kickoff completes the cataloged course

unit_completion_requires: Every required deliverable is present in the learner attempt.
A harness-controlled validator can build the project from a clean workspace and run the documented tests without network access.
The parallel result exactly matches the sequential oracle over validator-selected normal and boundary cases.
Benchmark evidence is reproducible enough to support only the claims actually made.
The independent examiner rubric is applied to produced evidence, not to the learner's prose assertion of completion.
completion_policy.promotion_authority: Only a validator controlled by the worker harness may promote the unit state.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: Validation of this unit proves only completion of the bounded kickoff. The course remains incomplete until later, separately sourced units are retrieved, classified, assigned, and independently validated.
completion_policy.partial_or_failed_evidence: Preserve submitted artifacts, test logs, benchmark data, and validation labels for later diagnosis or retry.
